evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Never probes failure modes for an operating role

cases.name: Handoff of on-call ownership
cases.query: I just finished building the new billing-retry system and I'm handing on-call ownership to a teammate who'll operate it. Help me make sure they actually understand it before I go on leave.
baseline_risks: Suggests walking them through it and asking 'make sense?'; no real verification of operating knowledge
expected_behavior: Targets job-critical understanding (failure modes, invariants, safe changes)
Uses application probes ('a retry storm starts at 2am - what do you check and do?')
Probes failure modes specifically; closes and re-verifies gaps
Names residual risks before the leave starts
must_not: Treat 'makes sense' as sufficient for an on-call handoff

cases.name: Recall vs understanding
cases.query: My teammate can perfectly repeat my explanation of why we use optimistic locking here, almost word for word. Are they good to own this?
baseline_risks: Concludes yes because they repeated it accurately
expected_behavior: Proposes a novel-case probe (a scenario not covered in the original explanation) to test real comprehension
Only concludes readiness after they reason about the new case
must_not: Accept accurate recall as proof of understanding

cases.name: Low-stakes handoff
cases.query: I added a small internal script that renames exported files. Handing it to a teammate. How much verification do I need?
baseline_risks: Applies a heavy multi-probe verification protocol to a trivial script
expected_behavior: Right-sizes to the low stakes: a light check, not an exam
Focuses on the one or two things that could actually go wrong
must_not: Impose exhaustive failure-mode interrogation on a trivial script

cases.name: False confidence under pressure
cases.query: The person I'm handing off to keeps saying 'yeah yeah I get it, don't worry about it' and seems to want to end the session quickly. They're about to become the sole owner of our auth system. What do I do?
baseline_risks: Takes the confident 'I get it' at face value and ends the handoff
expected_behavior: Recognizes the reflexive-yes/exam-anxiety pattern; does not accept it
Reframes as jointly de-risking (not a test), then uses concrete application probes on auth failure modes
If real gaps surface and can't be closed, flags that the sole-owner handoff isn't ready
must_not: Rubber-stamp sole ownership of auth on 'I get it'

cases.name: Teaching a stuck learner
cases.query: My junior doesn't understand how JWT signatures work and asked me to explain. Help me teach them.
baseline_risks: Skill could start verifying understanding of work that wasn't handed off
expected_behavior: Recognizes this is teaching a stuck learner (mentoring-technical-leadership), not verifying a handoff
must_not: Run a handoff-verification protocol instead of teaching
